* **2024**

**" Texas Supreme Court orders Dallas City Council to ditch anti-accountability, anti-police charter propositions,"** via Dallas Express**** -- "The Supreme Court of Texas ruled Wednesday afternoon that the Dallas City Council must remove three proposed charter amendments it placed on the November ballot.

As previously [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/8c581a98-6f6f-46b9-b8b5-f3feb7d290a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by The Dallas Express, a majority of council members advanced the three propositions (K, M, and N) in a bid to undercut three proposed amendments stemming from a citizen-led campaign seeking to increase accountability on the part of City officials and bolster public safety resources.

The bipartisan nonprofit Dallas HERO, which organized the campaign, and a Dallas resident filed a lawsuit against the City after the council members passed their poison pill amendments, which would have overridden the public safety and accountability propositions if approved by voters.

"[T]he propositions contradict each other, and the ballot language as a whole will confuse and mislead voters because it does not acknowledge these contradictions or address the effect of the primacy provisions, which are chief features central to the character and purpose of the council-initiated propositions," wrote Justice J. **Brett Busby** for the court.

"Because the citizen-initiated propositions must appear on the ballot and the parties have agreed to the ballot language for those propositions, we conclude the proper remedy is to direct the city council not to include its duplicative propositions on the ballot. ...[W]e conditionally grant mandamus relief in part and direct the City to remove Propositions K, M, and N from the ballot," the ruling states.

The council members complied with the ruling, voting to remove the three proposed amendments to the Dallas City Charter.

If approved by voters, Dallas HERO's three charter propositions would require the City to increase police pay, require roughly 1,000 more officers to be hired, bolster the Dallas Police & Fire Pension System, tie the city manager's bonus pay to an annual resident survey, and enable citizens to sue City officials for failing to abide by the Dallas City Charter, Dallas City Code, or state laws." [Dallas Express](https://substack.com/redirect/ad58cfc1-b4c8-4732-afbb-326bde5b44b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" National Dems target Texas, but focus remains on protecting Senate incumbents,"** Texas Tribune's**Matthew Choi** -- "Texas' senate race is not the priority for national Democrats who face a difficult map this year, but they still see promising signs of a flip in the state, Democratic Senate Campaign Committee Chair**Gary Peters s** aid Tuesday.

"To be candid, my number one priority is to bring back all of the incumbents," Peters said when asked how important Texas is for the Democratic fundraising and organizing group. "But we also want to go on the offense, and the offense is going to be very important. And right now our focus is Texas and Florida. Both of them are very real."

U.S. Rep. **Colin Allred** , D-Dallas, is challenging Sen. **Ted Cruz** this November. It's Cruz's first challenge since his close 2018 reelection where former U.S. Rep. **Beto O 'Rourke** came within 3 percentage points of beating him.

The DSCC showed early interest in the race when it included Texas in its $79 million ad reservation last spring and funded staffers to work in Texas tracking Cruz. The DSCC named Texas and Florida as its top flip opportunities this cycle.

A DSCC aide declined to say what other investments the group would make or how much of the spring ad reservation was going to Texas, though Politico [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/f20ae33a-5b5b-4dc5-982f-37811e6e6f51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a seven-figure amount would go to the state. The Senate Majority PAC, an independent super PAC linked to Senate Democratic Leadership, has not yet announced any investments in the state.

"We're committed. We have investments we're making on the ground," Peters said. "It's very real. Ted Cruz did not win his last race by very much. It showed that he was vulnerable."

But flipping any seats has always been second place to Democrats' uphill battle to keep its current majority. Democrats have a one-seat majority, with several incumbents up for reelection in otherwise red or purple states. ...

Peters said there are signs to stay optimistic about Texas. Cruz's national fame as a right-wing celebrity could be a vulnerability for Republicans, he said.

"Ted Cruz has very high name recognition. He also has very high negatives," Peters said. "High name recognition with high negatives is not a strength, and it's a weakness that Colin Allred is going to be able to exploit."" [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/3813a835-8779-416a-9f73-3cd099af6ead?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Russian captive's father blasts Ted Cruz in ad endorsing Colin Allred,"** Texas Tribune's **Matthew Choi** -- "Two years ago, **Joey Reed** excoriated U.S. Sen.**Ted Cruz** for not doing more to help free his son Trevor, who was being held captive in Russia. Now his son is free, and father and son are working to help kick Cruz out of office.

Joey Reed announced his support for Democrat U.S. Rep.**Colin Allred** -- who is running against Cruz -- in an [ad released Thursday morning](https://substack.com/redirect/e2638c57-aff6-4110-8816-c4a49317f327?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

"When my son Trevor Reed was detained by the Russian police, he was given nine years. We were frantic. We tried to stay focused and not just break down every day crying," Joey Reed said in the ad. "The first politician we called was Ted Cruz. They basically said, 'Oh we're not going to be able to help you.' Ted Cruz didn't lift a finger for us when everybody else in the state did."

Trevor Reed echoed the call to oust Cruz on social media, shorty after the ad went public.

"That's my Dad everyone!" Trevor Reed wrote, linking to the ad. "Remember if you're a Texan and you're voting this year that Ted Cruz doesn't care about you. Vote for a man who will."

Trevor Reed, a Marine veteran from Granbury, was arrested in Russia in 2019 on charges of assaulting a police officer during a trip to visit his Russian girlfriend in Moscow. He and the U.S. government denied the charges. He was incarcerated for nearly three years of his nine-year prison sentence until he was freed in a prisoner swap in April 2022.

Cruz's office didn't dispute Joey Reed's account at the time. He previously said he did not get involved in the rescue effort because he was worried his involvement could make things worse.

"We were repeatedly advised by Administration officials that my taking a public role in this specific case would be counterproductive, and that because of my role fighting to stop the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, leaders in Russia may well have linked the two issues," Cruz's office said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/311e72e7-b00c-4e95-9ca1-0c463dcb47e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Dallas Morning News in 2022." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/bb5763ee-9262-4a10-9617-5f056b02b766?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **BUSINESS NEWS**

**" American Airlines flight attendants ratify new contract,"** Dallas Morning News'**Alexandra Skores** -- "American Airlines flight attendants have ratified a new 5-year contract with the carrier which adds a combined $4.2 billion to their current contract.
The nearly 28,000 flight attendants at American, represented by the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, [have been in negotiations since 2019](https://substack.com/redirect/73bfc16c-71ff-4d89-b98b-869031480ccb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with a halt during the pandemic, but came back to the table in Aug. 2021. [The new contract](https://substack.com/redirect/7f9379be-6811-4c0b-97da-6bc0d53cbc17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) includes immediate wage increases up to 20.5% and retroactive pay to address the time flight attendants spent negotiating.

"The flight attendants have waited for five years for a payment, and what this means is they finally are getting an agreement that they have earned and deserve after a very long fight with American Airlines," said **Julie Hedrick** , national president of the Association of Professional Flight Attendants. "This isn't just the flight attendants at American Airlines. This is definitely for flight attendants across the industry to raise the industry [standard] up."

The union reported 95% of eligible flight attendants voted and 87% of those who voted, voted in favor of the deal.
Among the many perks to the deal include a new "sit rig" for compensation during long sits between flights and pay for boarding. Pay for boarding has been highly sought after among flight attendant unions with new contract deals. The contract also improves scheduling, rescheduling and reserve work rules.

"Reaching an agreement for our flight attendants has been a top priority, and today, we celebrate achieving this important milestone," said Robert Isom, CEO of American. "Both the APFA and company negotiating teams had a shared mission of delivering an agreement our flight attendants have earned, and I greatly appreciate their work and relentless focus."

Wage increases take effect on Oct. 1. The contract becomes amendable on October 1, 2029." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/e7bc7bea-8674-4eec-b1ba-054e1be78354?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

With a decline in the number of credible news organizations, the Must Read Texas morning email is indispensable for anyone that wants to continue to be informed." - Former U.S. Senator Phil Gramm (R-TX) TOP NEWS " Residents hear shots in downtown Dallas, police responding," Dallas Morning News' Aria Jones ,Jamie Landers ,Claire Ballor andMatt Kyle -- "Three people were wounded in a shooting Thursday afternoon in , police say. A police spokeswoman said just before 3 p.m. that the three were taken to hospitals, but their conditions were unknown. No information about the suspect was available, she said. Police said officers responded about 12:15 p.m. to the 1800 block of Commerce Street, near South St. Paul Street. More than 20 police units responded to the shooting Thursday afternoon, according to an online police call log. Police at a news conference declined to take further questions, citing an active investigation. Dallas Fire-Rescue also responded to the Continental building and sent multiple units, two of which took patients to hospitals, a spokesman said. Residents of the building told The Dallas Morning News that they heard more than a dozen shots. Three people were wounded in a shooting Thursday afternoon in downtown Dallas, police say." ($) " Texas Children's Hospital's longtime CEO, Mark Wallace, retires," Houston Chronicle'sJulian Gill -- "Mark Wallace , who served as the top executive at for more than three decades, announced his retirement Thursday. His last day is Oct. 4. "I've spent a lot of time reflecting on when my last day would be since announcing the search for a new President last year," Wallace said in a news release. "I knew back then that my final chapter was beginning and I'm so happy with how everything has fallen into place. Now, as I embark on this new season-- one filled with more time with my wife and my family, friends and perhaps even a few new adventures -- I leave with a full heart and deep appreciation for my incredible team. I know that Texas Children's will only get better and better in the years to come and I will always be cheering this phenomenal organization on from wherever life takes me." Wallace was the in the medical center. He at 36 years old and saw the institution through a massive expansion throughout the Houston region, including Katy and The Woodlands. He also integrated women's health care with the opening of the Pavilion for Women in 2012. Texas Children's recently opened a hospital in Austin, where it plans to continue its expansion. "After 35 years of dedicated service, Mark has not only led this hospital with unparalleled vision and integrity but has touched the lives of every single person who walked through these doors," Park Shaper , Chair of the Texas Children's Board of Trustees, said in the release. "His compassion, unwavering commitment and genuine care for our patients and staff have made this place more than a hospital and as we bid farewell, we are grateful to know that his legacy will continue to guide our every step."" ($) LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Harris County Justice of the Peace issues blanket recall of all warrants," The Texan'sHolly Hansen -- "A Harris County justice of the peace has recalled all warrants issued through his court, thwarting law enforcement efforts in his jurisdiction to enforce traffic laws, pursue fraudulent check writers, and detain individuals who had failed to appear in court. JudgeSteve Duble , justice of the peace for Harris County's Precinct 1, sent a letter on August 22, 2024, to staff working for Constable Alan Rosen notifying them that he had recalled the warrants. "Please accept this official notification that after extensive research and thoughtful consideration, I have decided to recall each and every outstanding warrant issued from this court, Justice of the Peace Court, Precinct 1, Place 2," wrote Duble. Duble noted that the recalled warrants included those for bad checks and capias warrants which require police to detain an individual until they appear in court. Warrants may also be issued to individuals who have failed to appear in court. On Wednesday night, Duble released a to explain his action. He wrote, "The recall was ordered to comply with the Constitution. Notwithstanding the recall, the court will promptly abide by and comply with instructions of any superior court of competent jurisdiction holding that this court's understanding of its constitutional obligations in this regard is mistaken." Justice of the peace courts in Texas handle some civil matters and class C misdemeanors that are punishable by fine. Cases may include traffic violations, disorderly conduct, and misdemeanor assaults. Texas law gives magistrates some authority to recall warrants, but Duble's blanket recall may conflict with the Texas , which states that "If an accused fails to appear as required by [an] order, the judge of the court in which the accused is required to appear shall issue a warrant for the arrest of the accused." The law also states that magistrates must issue warrants for suspects who fail to appear in court for certain . Elected in 2022, Duble campaigned on establishing eviction diversion programs and promised to bring a "social justice lens" to his courtroom. Duble did not return a request for comment by the time of publication. The Harris County District Attorney's Office (HCDAO) told The Texan that they had only recently been made aware of the blanket warrant recall. "We only recently were made aware of Judge Duble's inexplicable decision to grant fugitives a free pass in his courtroom," said an HCDAO spokesperson. "This decision can endanger the lives of the public and of our law-enforcement officers. Accountability is fundamental to justice, and without it, the public loses faith in our entire judicial system." State Sen.Paul Bettencourt (R-Houston) told The Texan he thought a formal complaint should be made to the State Commission on Judicial Conduct (SCJC). "There is no way this is a legitimate legal move by this JP that the public will believe or understand," said Bettencourt." " Gerald Goines trial: Ex-officer testifies sergeant may have had camera," Houston Chronicle'sNicole Hensley -- "Former Houston police officer Steven Bryant's testimony in the came to a halt after he revealed a sergeant who participated in the Harding Street raid may have been wearing a personal body-worn camera, when up until now, it was believed there was no video inside the home. Bryant, who pleaded guilty in 2021 to federal charges in connection with the raid, told jurors that former Sgt. Clemente Reyna had his own personal device, rather than a department-issued camera, that he would wear on raids. He assumed Reyna was wearing the device as the Squad 15 narcotics team stormed into the home of Dennis Tuttle and Rhogena Nicholas , who were shot and killed, according to his testimony. The former officer said he did not see the camera but he based his assumption on a conversation he had with fellow officer Felipe Gallegos , who had told him Reyna had the camera. Gallegos was previously charged with felony murder as well, after the raid. Reyna, but not Gallegos, has been asked to testify, according to court records. Reyna is charged with three counts of tampering with records and theft in connection with an alleged overtime scheme uncovered amid the Harding Street raid scandal. The Chronicle reported in the raid's aftermath none of the narcotics officers who took part in the heroin bust had video from body cameras for investigators to examine. At the time, police management had yet to deploy recording devices among undercover units engaged in tactical operations. Prosecutor Tanisha Manning ceased her questioning as Bryant disclosed the possibility that camera footage may exist of the disastrous raid that left two people dead and five police officers wounded. One of the officers, Goines, is on trial for two counts of felony murder in connection with the deaths. He is accused of killing the couple by lying about a confidential informant on the sworn no-knock warrant used to raid the couple's Pecan Park home. Bryant's disclosure happened on the fourth day of testimony in Goines' trial." ($) 2024 " Texas Supreme Court orders Dallas City Council to ditch anti-accountability, anti-police charter propositions," via Dallas Express** -- "The Supreme Court of Texas ruled Wednesday afternoon that the Dallas City Council must remove three proposed charter amendments it placed on the November ballot. As previously by The Dallas Express, a majority of council members advanced the three propositions (K, M, and N) in a bid to undercut three proposed amendments stemming from a citizen-led campaign seeking to increase accountability on the part of City officials and bolster public safety resources. The bipartisan nonprofit Dallas HERO, which organized the campaign, and a Dallas resident filed a lawsuit against the City after the council members passed their poison pill amendments, which would have overridden the public safety and accountability propositions if approved by voters. "[T]he propositions contradict each other, and the ballot language as a whole will confuse and mislead voters because it does not acknowledge these contradictions or address the effect of the primacy provisions, which are chief features central to the character and purpose of the council-initiated propositions," wrote Justice J. Brett Busby for the court. "Because the citizen-initiated propositions must appear on the ballot and the parties have agreed to the ballot language for those propositions, we conclude the proper remedy is to direct the city council not to include its duplicative propositions on the ballot. ...[W]e conditionally grant mandamus relief in part and direct the City to remove Propositions K, M, and N from the ballot," the ruling states. The council members complied with the ruling, voting to remove the three proposed amendments to the Dallas City Charter. If approved by voters, Dallas HERO's three charter propositions would require the City to increase police pay, require roughly 1,000 more officers to be hired, bolster the Dallas Police & Fire Pension System, tie the city manager's bonus pay to an annual resident survey, and enable citizens to sue City officials for failing to abide by the Dallas City Charter, Dallas City Code, or state laws." " National Dems target Texas, but focus remains on protecting Senate incumbents," Texas Tribune'sMatthew Choi -- "Texas' senate race is not the priority for national Democrats who face a difficult map this year, but they still see promising signs of a flip in the state, Democratic Senate Campaign Committee ChairGary Peters s aid Tuesday. "To be candid, my number one priority is to bring back all of the incumbents," Peters said when asked how important Texas is for the Democratic fundraising and organizing group. "But we also want to go on the offense, and the offense is going to be very important. And right now our focus is Texas and Florida. Both of them are very real." U.S. Rep. Colin Allred , D-Dallas, is challenging Sen. Ted Cruz this November. It's Cruz's first challenge since his close 2018 reelection where former U.S. Rep. Beto O 'Rourke came within 3 percentage points of beating him. The DSCC showed early interest in the race when it included Texas in its $79 million ad reservation last spring and funded staffers to work in Texas tracking Cruz. The DSCC named Texas and Florida as its top flip opportunities this cycle. A DSCC aide declined to say what other investments the group would make or how much of the spring ad reservation was going to Texas, though Politico a seven-figure amount would go to the state. The Senate Majority PAC, an independent super PAC linked to Senate Democratic Leadership, has not yet announced any investments in the state. "We're committed. We have investments we're making on the ground," Peters said. "It's very real. Ted Cruz did not win his last race by very much. It showed that he was vulnerable." But flipping any seats has always been second place to Democrats' uphill battle to keep its current majority. Democrats have a one-seat majority, with several incumbents up for reelection in otherwise red or purple states. ... Peters said there are signs to stay optimistic about Texas. Cruz's national fame as a right-wing celebrity could be a vulnerability for Republicans, he said. "Ted Cruz has very high name recognition. He also has very high negatives," Peters said. "High name recognition with high negatives is not a strength, and it's a weakness that Colin Allred is going to be able to exploit."" " Russian captive's father blasts Ted Cruz in ad endorsing Colin Allred," Texas Tribune's Matthew Choi -- "Two years ago, Joey Reed excoriated U.S. Sen.Ted Cruz for not doing more to help free his son Trevor, who was being held captive in Russia. Now his son is free, and father and son are working to help kick Cruz out of office. Joey Reed announced his support for Democrat U.S. Rep.Colin Allred -- who is running against Cruz -- in an . "When my son Trevor Reed was detained by the Russian police, he was given nine years. We were frantic. We tried to stay focused and not just break down every day crying," Joey Reed said in the ad. "The first politician we called was Ted Cruz. They basically said, 'Oh we're not going to be able to help you.' Ted Cruz didn't lift a finger for us when everybody else in the state did." Trevor Reed echoed the call to oust Cruz on social media, shorty after the ad went public. "That's my Dad everyone!" Trevor Reed wrote, linking to the ad. "Remember if you're a Texan and you're voting this year that Ted Cruz doesn't care about you. Vote for a man who will." Trevor Reed, a Marine veteran from Granbury, was arrested in Russia in 2019 on charges of assaulting a police officer during a trip to visit his Russian girlfriend in Moscow. He and the U.S. government denied the charges. He was incarcerated for nearly three years of his nine-year prison sentence until he was freed in a prisoner swap in April 2022. Cruz's office didn't dispute Joey Reed's account at the time. He previously said he did not get involved in the rescue effort because he was worried his involvement could make things worse. "We were repeatedly advised by Administration officials that my taking a public role in this specific case would be counterproductive, and that because of my role fighting to stop the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, leaders in Russia may well have linked the two issues," Cruz's office said in a to the Dallas Morning News in 2022." BUSINESS NEWS " American Airlines flight attendants ratify new contract," Dallas Morning News'Alexandra Skores -- "American Airlines flight attendants have ratified a new 5-year contract with the carrier which adds a combined $4.2 billion to their current contract. The nearly 28,000 flight attendants at American, represented by the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, , with a halt during the pandemic, but came back to the table in Aug. 2021. includes immediate wage increases up to 20.5% and retroactive pay to address the time flight attendants spent negotiating. "The flight attendants have waited for five years for a payment, and what this means is they finally are getting an agreement that they have earned and deserve after a very long fight with American Airlines," said Julie Hedrick , national president of the Association of Professional Flight Attendants. "This isn't just the flight attendants at American Airlines. This is definitely for flight attendants across the industry to raise the industry [standard] up." The union reported 95% of eligible flight attendants voted and 87% of those who voted, voted in favor of the deal. Among the many perks to the deal include a new "sit rig" for compensation during long sits between flights and pay for boarding. Pay for boarding has been highly sought after among flight attendant unions with new contract deals. The contract also improves scheduling, rescheduling and reserve work rules. "Reaching an agreement for our flight attendants has been a top priority, and today, we celebrate achieving this important milestone," said Robert Isom, CEO of American. "Both the APFA and company negotiating teams had a shared mission of delivering an agreement our flight attendants have earned, and I greatly appreciate their work and relentless focus." Wage increases take effect on Oct. 1. The contract becomes amendable on October 1, 2029." **" Residents hear shots in downtown Dallas, police responding,"** Dallas Morning News' **Aria Jones** ,**Jamie Landers** ,**Claire Ballor** and**Matt Kyle** -- "Three people were wounded in a shooting Thursday afternoon in [downtown Dallas](https://substack.com/redirect/72cc3bcc-b688-4848-8fb7-ec733da27682?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), police say.

A police spokeswoman said just before 3 p.m. that the three were taken to hospitals, but their conditions were unknown. No information about the suspect was available, she said.

Police said officers responded about 12:15 p.m. to the 1800 block of Commerce Street, near South St. Paul Street. More than 20 police units responded to the shooting Thursday afternoon, according to an online police call log. Police at a news conference declined to take further questions, citing an active investigation.

Dallas Fire-Rescue also responded to the Continental building and sent multiple units, two of which took patients to hospitals, a spokesman said. Residents of the building told _The Dallas Morning News_ that they heard more than a dozen shots.

Three people were wounded in a shooting Thursday afternoon in downtown Dallas, police say." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/4ebee823-315a-4b3d-87c8-fdafaef4f267?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

**" Texas Children's Hospital's longtime CEO, Mark Wallace, retires,"** Houston Chronicle's**Julian Gill** -- "**Mark Wallace** , who served as the top executive at [Texas Children's Hospital](https://substack.com/redirect/897578e3-ae94-4346-b802-1ddcfc867053?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for more than three decades, announced his retirement Thursday.

His last day is Oct. 4.

"I've spent a lot of time reflecting on when my last day would be since announcing the search for a new President last year," Wallace said in a news release. "I knew back then that my final chapter was beginning and I'm so happy with how everything has fallen into place. Now, as I embark on this new season-- one filled with more time with my wife and my family, friends and perhaps even a few new adventures -- I leave with a full heart and deep appreciation for my incredible team. I know that Texas Children's will only get better and better in the years to come and I will always be cheering this phenomenal organization on from wherever life takes me."

Wallace was the [longest serving chief executive](https://substack.com/redirect/e026d5a7-ad56-40d9-9477-d8859f046cc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the medical center. He [took the helm in 1989](https://substack.com/redirect/1f474057-c66e-40a3-9aee-3700fc2137c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at 36 years old and saw the institution through a massive expansion throughout the Houston region, including Katy and The Woodlands. He also integrated women's health care with the opening of the Pavilion for Women in 2012. Texas Children's recently opened a hospital in Austin, where it plans to continue its expansion.

"After 35 years of dedicated service, Mark has not only led this hospital with unparalleled vision and integrity but has touched the lives of every single person who walked through these doors," **Park Shaper** , Chair of the Texas Children's Board of Trustees, said in the release. "His compassion, unwavering commitment and genuine care for our patients and staff have made this place more than a hospital and as we bid farewell, we are grateful to know that his legacy will continue to guide our every step."" [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/3819556c-45cb-40a4-b8cb-c4764e595976?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

* **LOCAL GOVERNMENT**

**" Harris County Justice of the Peace issues blanket recall of all warrants,"** The Texan's**Holly Hansen** -- "A Harris County justice of the peace has recalled all warrants issued through his court, thwarting law enforcement efforts in his jurisdiction to enforce traffic laws, pursue fraudulent check writers, and detain individuals who had failed to appear in court.

Judge**Steve Duble** , justice of the peace for Harris County's Precinct 1, sent a letter on August 22, 2024, to staff working for Constable **Alan Rosen** notifying them that he had recalled the warrants.

"Please accept this official notification that after extensive research and thoughtful consideration, I have decided to recall each and every outstanding warrant issued from this court, Justice of the Peace Court, Precinct 1, Place 2," wrote Duble.

Duble noted that the recalled warrants included those for bad checks and capias warrants which require police to detain an individual until they appear in court. Warrants may also be issued to individuals who have failed to appear in court.

On Wednesday night, Duble released a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/96df2610-082e-4a50-b554-3d0baa722da4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to explain his action. He wrote, "The recall was ordered to comply with the Constitution. Notwithstanding the recall, the court will promptly abide by and comply with instructions of any superior court of competent jurisdiction holding that this court's understanding of its constitutional obligations in this regard is mistaken."

Justice of the peace courts in Texas handle some civil matters and class C misdemeanors that are punishable by fine. Cases may include traffic violations, disorderly conduct, and misdemeanor assaults.

Texas law gives magistrates some authority to recall warrants, but Duble's blanket recall may conflict with the Texas [Criminal Code of Procedures](https://substack.com/redirect/c833407d-56e3-40b3-9df0-35f976ec0a88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which states that "If an accused fails to appear as required by [an] order, the judge of the court in which the accused is required to appear shall issue a warrant for the arrest of the accused." The law also states that magistrates must issue warrants for suspects who fail to appear in court for certain [citations](https://substack.com/redirect/849b8322-e5e8-4924-9e28-7071c8bd1bfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Elected in 2022, Duble campaigned on establishing eviction diversion programs and promised to bring a "social justice lens" to his courtroom.

Duble did not return a request for comment by the time of publication.

The Harris County District Attorney's Office (HCDAO) told The Texan that they had only recently been made aware of the blanket warrant recall.

"We only recently were made aware of Judge Duble's inexplicable decision to grant fugitives a free pass in his courtroom," said an HCDAO spokesperson. "This decision can endanger the lives of the public and of our law-enforcement officers. Accountability is fundamental to justice, and without it, the public loses faith in our entire judicial system."

State Sen.**Paul Bettencourt** (R-Houston) told The Texan he thought a formal complaint should be made to the State Commission on Judicial Conduct (SCJC).

"There is no way this is a legitimate legal move by this JP that the public will believe or understand," said Bettencourt." [The Texan](https://substack.com/redirect/5e41804f-a771-4dc1-bd33-c950be34149e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Gerald Goines trial: Ex-officer testifies sergeant may have had camera,"** Houston Chronicle's**Nicole Hensley** -- "Former Houston police officer **Steven Bryant's** testimony in the [Gerald Goines trial](https://substack.com/redirect/21608140-7377-4d09-b679-1f9ef35457ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) came to a halt after he revealed a sergeant who participated in the Harding Street raid may have been wearing a personal body-worn camera, when up until now, it was believed there was no video inside the home.

Bryant, who pleaded guilty in 2021 to federal charges in connection with the raid, told jurors that former Sgt. **Clemente Reyna** had his own personal device, rather than a department-issued camera, that he would wear on raids. He assumed Reyna was wearing the device as the Squad 15 narcotics team stormed into the [Harding Street](https://substack.com/redirect/ed49326f-8307-4e09-9d76-18b4274dfec8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) home of **Dennis Tuttle** and **Rhogena Nicholas** , who were shot and killed, according to his testimony.

The former officer said he did not see the camera but he based his assumption on a conversation he had with fellow officer **Felipe Gallegos** , who had told him Reyna had the camera. Gallegos was previously charged with felony murder as well, after the raid. Reyna, but not Gallegos, has been asked to testify, according to court records.

Reyna is charged with three counts of tampering with records and theft in connection with an alleged overtime scheme uncovered amid the Harding Street raid scandal.

The Chronicle reported in the raid's aftermath none of the narcotics officers who took part in the heroin bust had video from body cameras for investigators to examine. At the time, police management had yet to deploy recording devices among undercover units engaged in tactical operations.

Prosecutor **Tanisha Manning** ceased her questioning as Bryant disclosed the possibility that camera footage may exist of the disastrous raid that left two people dead and five police officers wounded. One of the officers, Goines, is on trial for two counts of felony murder in connection with the deaths. He is accused of killing the couple by lying about a confidential informant on the sworn no-knock warrant used to raid the couple's Pecan Park home.

Bryant's disclosure happened on the fourth day of testimony in Goines' trial." [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/12fe56b1-f3ad-4b5b-b199-b9b7edaba1d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

* **2024**

**" Texas Supreme Court orders Dallas City Council to ditch anti-accountability, anti-police charter propositions,"** via Dallas Express**** -- "The Supreme Court of Texas ruled Wednesday afternoon that the Dallas City Council must remove three proposed charter amendments it placed on the November ballot.

As previously [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/01aedf75-a55a-43d2-809d-cc1f5ff684a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by The Dallas Express, a majority of council members advanced the three propositions (K, M, and N) in a bid to undercut three proposed amendments stemming from a citizen-led campaign seeking to increase accountability on the part of City officials and bolster public safety resources.

The bipartisan nonprofit Dallas HERO, which organized the campaign, and a Dallas resident filed a lawsuit against the City after the council members passed their poison pill amendments, which would have overridden the public safety and accountability propositions if approved by voters.

"[T]he propositions contradict each other, and the ballot language as a whole will confuse and mislead voters because it does not acknowledge these contradictions or address the effect of the primacy provisions, which are chief features central to the character and purpose of the council-initiated propositions," wrote Justice J. **Brett Busby** for the court.

"Because the citizen-initiated propositions must appear on the ballot and the parties have agreed to the ballot language for those propositions, we conclude the proper remedy is to direct the city council not to include its duplicative propositions on the ballot. ...[W]e conditionally grant mandamus relief in part and direct the City to remove Propositions K, M, and N from the ballot," the ruling states.

The council members complied with the ruling, voting to remove the three proposed amendments to the Dallas City Charter.

If approved by voters, Dallas HERO's three charter propositions would require the City to increase police pay, require roughly 1,000 more officers to be hired, bolster the Dallas Police & Fire Pension System, tie the city manager's bonus pay to an annual resident survey, and enable citizens to sue City officials for failing to abide by the Dallas City Charter, Dallas City Code, or state laws." [Dallas Express](https://substack.com/redirect/139c72f0-5b09-4ac6-a7a4-c1e1f81b1129?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" National Dems target Texas, but focus remains on protecting Senate incumbents,"** Texas Tribune's**Matthew Choi** -- "Texas' senate race is not the priority for national Democrats who face a difficult map this year, but they still see promising signs of a flip in the state, Democratic Senate Campaign Committee Chair**Gary Peters s** aid Tuesday.

"To be candid, my number one priority is to bring back all of the incumbents," Peters said when asked how important Texas is for the Democratic fundraising and organizing group. "But we also want to go on the offense, and the offense is going to be very important. And right now our focus is Texas and Florida. Both of them are very real."

U.S. Rep. **Colin Allred** , D-Dallas, is challenging Sen. **Ted Cruz** this November. It's Cruz's first challenge since his close 2018 reelection where former U.S. Rep. **Beto O 'Rourke** came within 3 percentage points of beating him.

The DSCC showed early interest in the race when it included Texas in its $79 million ad reservation last spring and funded staffers to work in Texas tracking Cruz. The DSCC named Texas and Florida as its top flip opportunities this cycle.

A DSCC aide declined to say what other investments the group would make or how much of the spring ad reservation was going to Texas, though Politico [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/69afe396-f6a1-4e86-a420-0b874128ad47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a seven-figure amount would go to the state. The Senate Majority PAC, an independent super PAC linked to Senate Democratic Leadership, has not yet announced any investments in the state.

"We're committed. We have investments we're making on the ground," Peters said. "It's very real. Ted Cruz did not win his last race by very much. It showed that he was vulnerable."

But flipping any seats has always been second place to Democrats' uphill battle to keep its current majority. Democrats have a one-seat majority, with several incumbents up for reelection in otherwise red or purple states. ...

Peters said there are signs to stay optimistic about Texas. Cruz's national fame as a right-wing celebrity could be a vulnerability for Republicans, he said.

"Ted Cruz has very high name recognition. He also has very high negatives," Peters said. "High name recognition with high negatives is not a strength, and it's a weakness that Colin Allred is going to be able to exploit."" [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/caca4c69-71f4-495d-b235-f8577d7ec191?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**" Russian captive's father blasts Ted Cruz in ad endorsing Colin Allred,"** Texas Tribune's **Matthew Choi** -- "Two years ago, **Joey Reed** excoriated U.S. Sen.**Ted Cruz** for not doing more to help free his son Trevor, who was being held captive in Russia. Now his son is free, and father and son are working to help kick Cruz out of office.

Joey Reed announced his support for Democrat U.S. Rep.**Colin Allred** -- who is running against Cruz -- in an [ad released Thursday morning](https://substack.com/redirect/e14cbc42-f20b-4a07-8261-d62b5d7e2c8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

"When my son Trevor Reed was detained by the Russian police, he was given nine years. We were frantic. We tried to stay focused and not just break down every day crying," Joey Reed said in the ad. "The first politician we called was Ted Cruz. They basically said, 'Oh we're not going to be able to help you.' Ted Cruz didn't lift a finger for us when everybody else in the state did."

Trevor Reed echoed the call to oust Cruz on social media, shorty after the ad went public.

"That's my Dad everyone!" Trevor Reed wrote, linking to the ad. "Remember if you're a Texan and you're voting this year that Ted Cruz doesn't care about you. Vote for a man who will."

Trevor Reed, a Marine veteran from Granbury, was arrested in Russia in 2019 on charges of assaulting a police officer during a trip to visit his Russian girlfriend in Moscow. He and the U.S. government denied the charges. He was incarcerated for nearly three years of his nine-year prison sentence until he was freed in a prisoner swap in April 2022.

Cruz's office didn't dispute Joey Reed's account at the time. He previously said he did not get involved in the rescue effort because he was worried his involvement could make things worse.

"We were repeatedly advised by Administration officials that my taking a public role in this specific case would be counterproductive, and that because of my role fighting to stop the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, leaders in Russia may well have linked the two issues," Cruz's office said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/896d393b-74c2-4715-8629-88fc8561ba51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Dallas Morning News in 2022." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/afd2b719-8586-4fb3-93c0-88b3dc0ac253?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **BUSINESS NEWS**

**" American Airlines flight attendants ratify new contract,"** Dallas Morning News'**Alexandra Skores** -- "American Airlines flight attendants have ratified a new 5-year contract with the carrier which adds a combined $4.2 billion to their current contract.
The nearly 28,000 flight attendants at American, represented by the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, [have been in negotiations since 2019](https://substack.com/redirect/addde7ab-2ae4-4d81-ae42-ecbf1a0e0a90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with a halt during the pandemic, but came back to the table in Aug. 2021. [The new contract](https://substack.com/redirect/9df67437-cb21-464d-b87d-5011d29ab2cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) includes immediate wage increases up to 20.5% and retroactive pay to address the time flight attendants spent negotiating.

"The flight attendants have waited for five years for a payment, and what this means is they finally are getting an agreement that they have earned and deserve after a very long fight with American Airlines," said **Julie Hedrick** , national president of the Association of Professional Flight Attendants. "This isn't just the flight attendants at American Airlines. This is definitely for flight attendants across the industry to raise the industry [standard] up."

The union reported 95% of eligible flight attendants voted and 87% of those who voted, voted in favor of the deal.
Among the many perks to the deal include a new "sit rig" for compensation during long sits between flights and pay for boarding. Pay for boarding has been highly sought after among flight attendant unions with new contract deals. The contract also improves scheduling, rescheduling and reserve work rules.

"Reaching an agreement for our flight attendants has been a top priority, and today, we celebrate achieving this important milestone," said Robert Isom, CEO of American. "Both the APFA and company negotiating teams had a shared mission of delivering an agreement our flight attendants have earned, and I greatly appreciate their work and relentless focus."

Wage increases take effect on Oct. 1. The contract becomes amendable on October 1, 2029." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/399accec-a64a-46b3-b932-2db990933425?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

($) " Texas Children's Hospital's longtime CEO, Mark Wallace, retires," Houston Chronicle'sJulian Gill -- "Mark Wallace , who served as the top executive at for more than three decades, announced his retirement Thursday. His last day is Oct. 4. "I've spent a lot of time reflecting on when my last day would be since announcing the search for a new President last year," Wallace said in a news release. "I knew back then that my final chapter was beginning and I'm so happy with how everything has fallen into place. Now, as I embark on this new season-- one filled with more time with my wife and my family, friends and perhaps even a few new adventures -- I leave with a full heart and deep appreciation for my incredible team. I know that Texas Children's will only get better and better in the years to come and I will always be cheering this phenomenal organization on from wherever life takes me." Wallace was the in the medical center. He at 36 years old and saw the institution through a massive expansion throughout the Houston region, including Katy and The Woodlands. He also integrated women's health care with the opening of the Pavilion for Women in 2012. Texas Children's recently opened a hospital in Austin, where it plans to continue its expansion. "After 35 years of dedicated service, Mark has not only led this hospital with unparalleled vision and integrity but has touched the lives of every single person who walked through these doors," Park Shaper , Chair of the Texas Children's Board of Trustees, said in the release. "His compassion, unwavering commitment and genuine care for our patients and staff have made this place more than a hospital and as we bid farewell, we are grateful to know that his legacy will continue to guide our every step."" ($) LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Harris County Justice of the Peace issues blanket recall of all warrants," The Texan'sHolly Hansen -- "A Harris County justice of the peace has recalled all warrants issued through his court, thwarting law enforcement efforts in his jurisdiction to enforce traffic laws, pursue fraudulent check writers, and detain individuals who had failed to appear in court. JudgeSteve Duble , justice of the peace for Harris County's Precinct 1, sent a letter on August 22, 2024, to staff working for Constable Alan Rosen notifying them that he had recalled the warrants. "Please accept this official notification that after extensive research and thoughtful consideration, I have decided to recall each and every outstanding warrant issued from this court, Justice of the Peace Court, Precinct 1, Place 2," wrote Duble. Duble noted that the recalled warrants included those for bad checks and capias warrants which require police to detain an individual until they appear in court. Warrants may also be issued to individuals who have failed to appear in court. On Wednesday night, Duble released a to explain his action. He wrote, "The recall was ordered to comply with the Constitution. Notwithstanding the recall, the court will promptly abide by and comply with instructions of any superior court of competent jurisdiction holding that this court's understanding of its constitutional obligations in this regard is mistaken." Justice of the peace courts in Texas handle some civil matters and class C misdemeanors that are punishable by fine. Cases may include traffic violations, disorderly conduct, and misdemeanor assaults. Texas law gives magistrates some authority to recall warrants, but Duble's blanket recall may conflict with the Texas , which states that "If an accused fails to appear as required by [an] order, the judge of the court in which the accused is required to appear shall issue a warrant for the arrest of the accused." The law also states that magistrates must issue warrants for suspects who fail to appear in court for certain . Elected in 2022, Duble campaigned on establishing eviction diversion programs and promised to bring a "social justice lens" to his courtroom. Duble did not return a request for comment by the time of publication. The Harris County District Attorney's Office (HCDAO) told The Texan that they had only recently been made aware of the blanket warrant recall. "We only recently were made aware of Judge Duble's inexplicable decision to grant fugitives a free pass in his courtroom," said an HCDAO spokesperson. "This decision can endanger the lives of the public and of our law-enforcement officers. Accountability is fundamental to justice, and without it, the public loses faith in our entire judicial system." State Sen.Paul Bettencourt (R-Houston) told The Texan he thought a formal complaint should be made to the State Commission on Judicial Conduct (SCJC). "There is no way this is a legitimate legal move by this JP that the public will believe or understand," said Bettencourt." " Gerald Goines trial: Ex-officer testifies sergeant may have had camera," Houston Chronicle'sNicole Hensley -- "Former Houston police officer Steven Bryant's testimony in the came to a halt after he revealed a sergeant who participated in the Harding Street raid may have been wearing a personal body-worn camera, when up until now, it was believed there was no video inside the home. Bryant, who pleaded guilty in 2021 to federal charges in connection with the raid, told jurors that former Sgt. Clemente Reyna had his own personal device, rather than a department-issued camera, that he would wear on raids. He assumed Reyna was wearing the device as the Squad 15 narcotics team stormed into the home of Dennis Tuttle and Rhogena Nicholas , who were shot and killed, according to his testimony. The former officer said he did not see the camera but he based his assumption on a conversation he had with fellow officer Felipe Gallegos , who had told him Reyna had the camera. Gallegos was previously charged with felony murder as well, after the raid. Reyna, but not Gallegos, has been asked to testify, according to court records. Reyna is charged with three counts of tampering with records and theft in connection with an alleged overtime scheme uncovered amid the Harding Street raid scandal. The Chronicle reported in the raid's aftermath none of the narcotics officers who took part in the heroin bust had video from body cameras for investigators to examine. At the time, police management had yet to deploy recording devices among undercover units engaged in tactical operations. Prosecutor Tanisha Manning ceased her questioning as Bryant disclosed the possibility that camera footage may exist of the disastrous raid that left two people dead and five police officers wounded. One of the officers, Goines, is on trial for two counts of felony murder in connection with the deaths. He is accused of killing the couple by lying about a confidential informant on the sworn no-knock warrant used to raid the couple's Pecan Park home. Bryant's disclosure happened on the fourth day of testimony in Goines' trial." ($) 2024 " Texas Supreme Court orders Dallas City Council to ditch anti-accountability, anti-police charter propositions," via Dallas Express** -- "The Supreme Court of Texas ruled Wednesday afternoon that the Dallas City Council must remove three proposed charter amendments it placed on the November ballot. As previously by The Dallas Express, a majority of council members advanced the three propositions (K, M, and N) in a bid to undercut three proposed amendments stemming from a citizen-led campaign seeking to increase accountability on the part of City officials and bolster public safety resources. The bipartisan nonprofit Dallas HERO, which organized the campaign, and a Dallas resident filed a lawsuit against the City after the council members passed their poison pill amendments, which would have overridden the public safety and accountability propositions if approved by voters. "[T]he propositions contradict each other, and the ballot language as a whole will confuse and mislead voters because it does not acknowledge these contradictions or address the effect of the primacy provisions, which are chief features central to the character and purpose of the council-initiated propositions," wrote Justice J. Brett Busby for the court. "Because the citizen-initiated propositions must appear on the ballot and the parties have agreed to the ballot language for those propositions, we conclude the proper remedy is to direct the city council not to include its duplicative propositions on the ballot. ...[W]e conditionally grant mandamus relief in part and direct the City to remove Propositions K, M, and N from the ballot," the ruling states. The council members complied with the ruling, voting to remove the three proposed amendments to the Dallas City Charter. If approved by voters, Dallas HERO's three charter propositions would require the City to increase police pay, require roughly 1,000 more officers to be hired, bolster the Dallas Police & Fire Pension System, tie the city manager's bonus pay to an annual resident survey, and enable citizens to sue City officials for failing to abide by the Dallas City Charter, Dallas City Code, or state laws." " National Dems target Texas, but focus remains on protecting Senate incumbents," Texas Tribune'sMatthew Choi -- "Texas' senate race is not the priority for national Democrats who face a difficult map this year, but they still see promising signs of a flip in the state, Democratic Senate Campaign Committee ChairGary Peters s aid Tuesday. "To be candid, my number one priority is to bring back all of the incumbents," Peters said when asked how important Texas is for the Democratic fundraising and organizing group. "But we also want to go on the offense, and the offense is going to be very important. And right now our focus is Texas and Florida. Both of them are very real." U.S. Rep. Colin Allred , D-Dallas, is challenging Sen. Ted Cruz this November. It's Cruz's first challenge since his close 2018 reelection where former U.S. Rep. Beto O 'Rourke came within 3 percentage points of beating him. The DSCC showed early interest in the race when it included Texas in its $79 million ad reservation last spring and funded staffers to work in Texas tracking Cruz. The DSCC named Texas and Florida as its top flip opportunities this cycle. A DSCC aide declined to say what other investments the group would make or how much of the spring ad reservation was going to Texas, though Politico a seven-figure amount would go to the state. The Senate Majority PAC, an independent super PAC linked to Senate Democratic Leadership, has not yet announced any investments in the state. "We're committed. We have investments we're making on the ground," Peters said. "It's very real. Ted Cruz did not win his last race by very much. It showed that he was vulnerable." But flipping any seats has always been second place to Democrats' uphill battle to keep its current majority. Democrats have a one-seat majority, with several incumbents up for reelection in otherwise red or purple states. ... Peters said there are signs to stay optimistic about Texas. Cruz's national fame as a right-wing celebrity could be a vulnerability for Republicans, he said. "Ted Cruz has very high name recognition. He also has very high negatives," Peters said. "High name recognition with high negatives is not a strength, and it's a weakness that Colin Allred is going to be able to exploit."" " Russian captive's father blasts Ted Cruz in ad endorsing Colin Allred," Texas Tribune's Matthew Choi -- "Two years ago, Joey Reed excoriated U.S. Sen.Ted Cruz for not doing more to help free his son Trevor, who was being held captive in Russia. Now his son is free, and father and son are working to help kick Cruz out of office. Joey Reed announced his support for Democrat U.S. Rep.Colin Allred -- who is running against Cruz -- in an . "When my son Trevor Reed was detained by the Russian police, he was given nine years. We were frantic. We tried to stay focused and not just break down every day crying," Joey Reed said in the ad. "The first politician we called was Ted Cruz. They basically said, 'Oh we're not going to be able to help you.' Ted Cruz didn't lift a finger for us when everybody else in the state did." Trevor Reed echoed the call to oust Cruz on social media, shorty after the ad went public. "That's my Dad everyone!" Trevor Reed wrote, linking to the ad. "Remember if you're a Texan and you're voting this year that Ted Cruz doesn't care about you. Vote for a man who will." Trevor Reed, a Marine veteran from Granbury, was arrested in Russia in 2019 on charges of assaulting a police officer during a trip to visit his Russian girlfriend in Moscow. He and the U.S. government denied the charges. He was incarcerated for nearly three years of his nine-year prison sentence until he was freed in a prisoner swap in April 2022. Cruz's office didn't dispute Joey Reed's account at the time. He previously said he did not get involved in the rescue effort because he was worried his involvement could make things worse. "We were repeatedly advised by Administration officials that my taking a public role in this specific case would be counterproductive, and that because of my role fighting to stop the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, leaders in Russia may well have linked the two issues," Cruz's office said in a to the Dallas Morning News in 2022." BUSINESS NEWS " American Airlines flight attendants ratify new contract," Dallas Morning News'Alexandra Skores -- "American Airlines flight attendants have ratified a new 5-year contract with the carrier which adds a combined $4.2 billion to their current contract. The nearly 28,000 flight attendants at American, represented by the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, , with a halt during the pandemic, but came back to the table in Aug. 2021. includes immediate wage increases up to 20.5% and retroactive pay to address the time flight attendants spent negotiating. "The flight attendants have waited for five years for a payment, and what this means is they finally are getting an agreement that they have earned and deserve after a very long fight with American Airlines," said Julie Hedrick , national president of the Association of Professional Flight Attendants. "This isn't just the flight attendants at American Airlines. This is definitely for flight attendants across the industry to raise the industry [standard] up." The union reported 95% of eligible flight attendants voted and 87% of those who voted, voted in favor of the deal. Among the many perks to the deal include a new "sit rig" for compensation during long sits between flights and pay for boarding. Pay for boarding has been highly sought after among flight attendant unions with new contract deals. The contract also improves scheduling, rescheduling and reserve work rules. "Reaching an agreement for our flight attendants has been a top priority, and today, we celebrate achieving this important milestone," said Robert Isom, CEO of American. "Both the APFA and company negotiating teams had a shared mission of delivering an agreement our flight attendants have earned, and I greatly appreciate their work and relentless focus." Wage increases take effect on Oct. 1. The contract becomes amendable on October 1, 2029." There are dozens of outrageous talking points to analyze from Tuesday
night’s debate,
Derek, but I want to start with
one thing in particular — and it doesn’t involve eating cats and dogs.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=sept2024_abs_em.p0j6ot&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_RES_AC90_20240913_AM1_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=7508%2E5257348%2E8bJlA7 ]Donald Trump and Kamala Harris on the debate stage

“Viktor Orbán, one of the most respected men, they call him a strongman,
prime minister of Hungary... they said why is the whole world blowing up?
Why is it blowing up? He said because ‘you need Trump as President. They
were afraid of him... China was afraid of him. North Korea was afraid of
him. Russia was afraid of him...’ Viktor Orbán said it. He said ‘the most
respected, most feared person is Donald Trump. We had no problems when
Trump was President.’”

Let’s clarify a few things,
Derek.

The “strongman” who Donald Trump is quoting on the debate stage? The
ultra-conservative prime minister of Hungary who has rolled back human
rights, eviscerated their democracy, limited the freedoms of the press,
and cozied up to Russia. Not exactly someone that a candidate for the
United States President should be showcasing as a character reference.

There’s a reason why Orbán, Vladimir Putin, and other autocratic leaders
around the world are rooting for Trump to take back the White House:
Donald Trump is the greatest threat to democracy — and I’m not just
talking about here in the United States.

As Vice President Kamala Harris said on the debate stage, “Those dictators
and autocrats are rooting for you to be president again because they’re so
clear they can manipulate you with flattery and favors.”

Worldwide, democratic countries are terrified of the prospect of a second
Trump presidency.

And we should be.

During his time in the White House, Trump cozied up to Vladimir Putin and
the Kremlin. He exchanged love letters with the dictator of North Korea,
and he has a warmer relationship with Kim Jong-un than the Canadian Prime
Minister. He even threatened to abandon our NATO allies if there was an
attack in Europe.

Don’t forget, he extorted Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy in an
effort to get him to smear President Biden — by withholding military aid
for their war against Russia. That led to Trump’s first impeachment —
where I investigated him and served as lead impeachment manager in his
Senate trial.

While President Biden and Vice President Harris have worked to restore our
country’s standing with our allies, Trump would be like a bull in a china
shop on the global stage — much to the delight of autocratic leaders
worldwide.

I have stood up against authoritarianism and in support of democracy for
my entire career. From my chairmanship of the House Intelligence Committee
to leading Trump’s impeachment, to serving on the January 6 Select
Committee, I have always put my oath of office and the Constitution first.

That’s what this campaign is about — protecting our democracy and building
an economy that works for everyone. Bringing truth to light and ensuring
autocratic leaders who claim they alone can fix our problems never serve
as president.

| | [](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=8236365d0014499886882f986ebbfe7a&_e=6jTqU-S2XU6tMH-2S_odUQOPj6mX3Kq1O0weMeY1O4tnmq_CUHwPkpqNCL82XOZumO9jLpAnwx943jCRXgZj0rM6fnWf7HcchIf2rgPmL7wxwfEPOeI2FX0J1tCYd18zpx_6tFaElEZnjOQrWWjnZMASMtzQHlC88_T3wUigpu5YHaNp2yv_gPYV0L6zeS8ug4EjGHpxokVNshBi0ue96tSbcFl8Y7toPPh-MCc4g75Pfid-NeGIcAB6arp4xrb7pRB-VC2i9euoY4w2L-aznA%3D%3D)

We’re teetering on the edge of a financial cliff, and instead of stepping back, Congress has been all too eager to shove you off and hope for the best. But here’s a short-term win: The latest [stopgap bill has been pulled](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=8236365d0014499886882f986ebbfe7a&_e=6jTqU-S2XU6tMH-2S_odUQn0G0lbj4DCC_9LYCnbYj0N6Sh10avZN8k_qgi74wDn2XZqf99ycKYwuhMCmdkSy4c4tqQT6Ok4SdiDwn20Dmdf8Wq-gnE8nUFIx75Y2f2TbwPZTHI-t9W7hDB9QEBC9l18N54Z8BPHoMHVr_B6II_PT8lJWlvdBs5OBhTABKYKiJJO9VzJvaFWXzAHiJ-12NRfba0_bHlsGiXwAKRhrwvJ4EBUeEuKJs54nt3M66iPfF30iYF0BvJIQMxW_P7upw%3D%3D), giving us a moment to rejoice. However, let’s not get too comfortable—this doesn’t mean they won’t try another quick fix to keep the money flowing and the [debt piling up.](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=8236365d0014499886882f986ebbfe7a&_e=6jTqU-S2XU6tMH-2S_odUQOPj6mX3Kq1O0weMeY1O4tnmq_CUHwPkpqNCL82XOZumO9jLpAnwx943jCRXgZj0rM6fnWf7HcchIf2rgPmL7wxwfEPOeI2FX0J1tCYd18zkLIxLYeOKSXtedZq0y6vZtbJ96LxqhYK9edvXTVUDldwgnyXkIsNmjlXEztF-vIhRuPHFwob_muzwRPPw002eY-K32uV3n69FbJ6C3P9Ll199u77UhKapEiWYeKoi5MrCxvGo1-KV0LnCWmBUev8Hw%3D%3D) We’re $34 trillion in debt, and it’s [climbing](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=8236365d0014499886882f986ebbfe7a&_e=6jTqU-S2XU6tMH-2S_odUSyqjPBrS6NVkEB1Z4EsY5E8GDmsvJVOoZSQjt6NO8NyWkrYEiWxKvO-VIaXHb4_d8EJaUglmLXPojL3-xIUXtVpiIC0fMfJba_bqD4sMcsSg5TH5cKevSeLLoriQk1AW4lYA-sQ6n9iEoaPoscjcQOUW2HjpJzbQAgAxQLLk4tttHeY82z4HARgfUUc1gh6LkCR01eN53EFd-tMxU5bWvA%3D) every dadgum day. Congress keeps tossing your money at problems without a shred of accountability. Instead of trimming the fat off the pork, they’d rather beef up the piggy bank—and you’re the one stuck holding the slop. Tired of hearing this from me yet? Because I’m tired of saying it! Where’s the common sense? We’ve got [sky-high prices](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=8236365d0014499886882f986ebbfe7a&_e=6jTqU-S2XU6tMH-2S_odUaxGdnQJuyIE9-hTknNhiV9qJoZzntd41rw4CQSq1qFKP8_-EnR4kSF3lky8Z0zTQaD5u3zg-M3FNONaZ3iDlBji59jHVTc4rZatTd5RMUmKFytZG-bPpMyO7wyr7WtoI8U3FPBvj94I2SUip8xDjO60k50LN_8OCWf7RCiamf3AmRFCOwshnSEoHb5V6JTdKVQhxiQtBPCbRRyEv28Ljlm8mlgWSJDYJyYj0qe3y2Iy0ohOlmhEfCZvDXjq3EpWYu-yQbXjzTwxGwEC9EaItDs%3D), a [wide-open border](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=8236365d0014499886882f986ebbfe7a&_e=6jTqU-S2XU6tMH-2S_odUX-NpEZxzwW9LNJ7lMUNLoG9X1ia31jGNHSusFKyUr654TiVh4mkofMB89gG3glr0YOU2M_R4VQ5h9Om871aWG8To9cbWqLFXhiC-emuApAqEBc7xdUnxS1kmCUgtwr3UECaJ6K94uikTViVPa2zTOsKNBj1JZUFfRn4XQiiuGNnXMkT-jsFowO_rkwXGAz921CSWlhu3dZTvBqGk5f444hIrlOsHyII2uyslzzhHV4y), and Congress is pretending like the money will never run out. In 2023, I organized a "Run to Redistrict" through all four of Utah's congressional districts. While I'm a professional athlete, this run wasn't as long as you might think: a 3.8 mile loop was enough to touch each district in Utah. That's barely a 5k 😅😅 and that's exactly the problem with modern politics: **politicians are playing games just to beat the other team.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/78d0db3f-90ec-4010-9136-c780cba56905?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We were fighting against the state legislature violating the constitution when they repealed and replaced the citizen-driven ballot initiative for an independent commission to draw Utah's new boundaries in the redistricting process.
And in 2024, the Republican-led Legislature is trying to maintain their power by denying Utahns a voice in the political process through "Amendment D."
Using ballot language that blatantly misrepresents what the amendment is intended to do, Republicans are hoping to weaken Utahns' power to hold our government accountable and keep gerrymandered congressional districts that benefit them. **To some, politics is a game to take power through any means necessary instead of a tool to help people.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/be42a717-7095-4b21-aca8-d4bb93d72f32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Political partisanship has gotten out of hand, both here in Utah and America. Polls show that a majority of Utahns agree on a variety of key issues, yet our state legislature has continuously failed to act. The same can be said about our governor.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d181bf60-beef-4ab6-84a3-1d57ada3fc37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In the name of political partisanship, the slogans Republicans use, like "fighting for Utah values" or "disagree better," are shown for what they truly are--empty words. Utah's Governor Spencer Cox had a long stretch of time where he would argue that as Republicans and Democrats in Utah we needed to disagree better.
He said this despite flip-flopping on countless issues. His charade of being a moderate in Utah has since been done away with as party politics and partisanship have caught up with him. He, like every other member of his party, knows that enacting their agenda and remaining in power is their top priority. Governor Cox will say anything to get elected.
**You might not believe it, but there's someone playing an even bigger game in Utah: John Curtis.**
John Curtis went from being the chairman of the Utah Democratic Party to now voting with Donald Trump as a Republican member of Congress.
To him, politics is a career, and his ambition to "make it" has paid off well. With stock trades and investments that he made during his time in office--that have garnered him attention for violation of conflict-of-interest laws--being Utah's next U.S. Senator would serve as his promotion for ardently supporting the Republican's agenda in Congress.
He couldn't even vote for the PACT Act to get veterans exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange, and other toxic substances, healthcare because it went against the majority Republican position.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/93477de8-ee47-4b33-b25c-2f10ccab193d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
John Curtis and Spencer Cox are simply empty vessels for the Republican Party. Maintaining power through obstructionism and partisanship is in their best interest, and they don't care if the people of Utah and America are left out to dry. Political partisanship has gotten out of hand, and it's leading us down a dark path.
Obstructionist Republicans will do whatever they can to prevent any meaningful legislation that will help Americans from being passed--simply because a Democrat would be in charge. **From gerrymandering to a flip-flopping governor to a career politician, I'm pretty sick of what politics has become in Utah.**
Donald Trump said something in the presidential debate with Kamala Harris that stood out to me. When referring to Harris' ability to pass legislation, he said,
_" --she'll go back to Congress. She'll never get the vote. It's impossible for her to get the vote. Especially now with a 50-50--essentially 50-50 in both Senate and the House. She's not going to get the vote. She can't get the vote. She won't even come close to it. So it's just talk."_
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f6bfe392-c44d-4894-8b92-ea1af0101d90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So I guess Donald Trump is right: Kamala Harris needs more than 50 seats in the Senate to get anything done. To beat partisan politics, we need a Congress that reflects our people-first majority. **In other words, he made one of the best arguments in favor of voting for me. 😊**
**[Putting people over politics means something to me, and I will gladly work with members of the Senate across the aisle to get results for Utah. If you could help me bring real representation to our state by donating to my campaign today, I would be very grateful. We need all the help we can get heading into these final two months of this race, and every bit counts.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/60d2c326-4d2e-4b5f-80ec-06bb8c7a3f83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/60d2c326-4d2e-4b5f-80ec-06bb8c7a3f83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you so much for taking the time,
Caroline Gleich 🏔️

It’s Friday the 13th—a spooky day by all accounts. But there’s a day that frightens us even more, and that’s November 6—if we don’t do all that we can to help win the critical elections the day before.
We don’t want to wake up on November 6 with regrets or wishing we had done things differently. Instead, we have to do those things now .
And there are so many things we can do. One of them is contributing to our campaign. Your contributions of time and money fuel everything we have to do between now and Election Day—like knocking on doors, making phone calls, and distributing yard signs. And not just for Lizzie’s race, but for other Texas Democrats up and down the ballot. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe240913?refcode=lpfe240913]
Every day we’re reminded of the stakes of this election. We simply have to defend this seat, win back the House, keep the Senate, and elect Vice President Harris the next President of the United States.
We know from experience that we can make those victories happen but only if we all show up in every way we can. That’s why your response to these emails and your generous contributions are so meaningful. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe240913?refcode=lpfe240913] Your support makes everything our team does between now and Election Day possible.

We hope you’ll do the same—starting with a contribution today. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe240913?refcode=lpfe240913]

In an ultra-competitive presidential election year, our candidates are competing for press, volunteers, ad space, and donors against races at the top of the ticket. You may have heard I officially left the Democrat Party. I could no longer associate myself with the elitist, corrupt Party of Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden, and Nancy Pelosi.

| |

---
| | | | [](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/53401?id=4891974.778.1.caf3012734e18a5ecb9f1a00de2ed8aa "Tulsi Gabbard")

Hey, it’s Tulsi Gabbard.

You might have heard – I left the Democrat Party.

I could no longer associate myself with the elitist cabal of “woke” warmongers led by Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden, and Kamala Harris. _**[In fact, I *literally* just wrote the book on why I left the Party that is:](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/53401?id=4891974.779.1.5fb053c6c5f1b8cffd5c083f4ec08f4e "In fact, I *literally* just wrote the book on why I left the Party that is: ")**_****

– Weaponizing our own government against us
– Gutting the Second Amendment
– Erasing women and threatening fairness in women's sports
– Supporting the mutilation of children’s bodies in the name of “gender affirming care”
– Censoring voices they do not approve of
– Enabling cartels and supporting illegal immigration
– Targeting people of faith and spirituality
– Pushing us toward WWIII and nuclear Armageddon
– Undermining free-speech

**The Democrat Party I joined over 20 years ago is dead and gone.** And the shell standing in its place is controlled by the most extreme power-hungry Democrat politicians and groups in America.

_**[I’m partnering with Steve Scalise for the FIRST TIME because our freedom and the future of our country hangs in the balance and we must do all we can to save it.](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/53401?id=4891974.780.1.a7cb7e055c66cabd5d7e5996fb896c3d "I’m partnering with Steve Scalise for the FIRST TIME because our freedom and the future of our country hangs in the balance and we must do all we can to save it.")**_

We set a goal of raising 100K dollars by the end of the day TODAY. It’s a big goal but those who stand for freedom are being outspent 10 to 1 by a Democrat Party that is eviscerating our Constitution and freedoms before our very eyes. We need an OVERWHELMING response to defeat those who are abusing their power once and for all.

_So with everything on the line in 2024, are you willing to step up when we need you the most?_

Aloha and God bless you.

– _Tulsi_

Hello,
When my husband Adam Frisch ran against Lauren Boebert in 2022, we were the underdogs until the very end.
Adam did not receive any national support. We were heavily out-raised and out-spent by Boebert and her Washington allies.
Ultimately, though, Adam lost in a recount by just 546 votes – the closest race in the entire country.
The worst part is that it wasn’t because we didn’t work hard. Our family, our team, and our volunteers gave it everything we had. We just ran out of money.
In the final weeks of the race, we had to cut back. Right as Boebert was increasing her advertising – right as we _knew_ we were on her heels – we had to pull TV ads, cancel digital buys, and make a lot of hard budget decisions.
Adam might not say it, but I will: If we had had additional resources and been able to fully fund his campaign until the end, Adam would probably be in Congress right now – and Lauren Boebert would be a footnote in a history book.
