**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Cost of living, housing affordability are top concerns for Colorado residents](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Cost of living, housing and politics top the list of concerns for Coloradans this year, according to the Colorado Health Foundation’s annual pulse survey.
Of the 2,404 individuals surveyed, 19% identified cost of living and inflation as the most important issue facing the state, while 17% named housing affordability and 11% cited government and politics. Other top concerns included homelessness, immigration and public safety.
Immigration saw the highest change — a 12-point increase from last year’s survey. Responses for cost of living and housing increased 3 and 2 points, respectively.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado avoided big funding cuts for schools. But relief for districts could be short-lived](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado lawmakers recently passed a property tax bill but face economic challenges that could jeopardize increased school funding planned for next year.
* A new school funding formula, which aims to provide an additional $500 million for education over six years, is at risk due to tight state budget forecasts.
* State Senator Barbara Kirkmeyer expressed concerns about the state's ability to fund the new formula amid competing priorities and a projected budget shortfall.
* School funding in Colorado is constitutionally required to increase annually based on inflation and population growth, adding further strain to the budget. The final decision on implementing the new funding formula will depend on upcoming economic forecasts and the legislative session in 2025.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Shape the future of energy: AGNC survey calls for community voices in Northwest Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Associated Governments of Northwest Colorado (AGNC) is spearheading a transition from coal to alternative energy sources, gathering local input through a survey until September 16, 2024.
* Preliminary results from an AGNC survey indicate strong local support for nuclear energy as an alternative to coal.
* AGNC is working to develop a regional energy hub that blends traditional and renewable sources to preserve jobs and stabilize the local economy.
* The survey results will guide future energy policies to support communities affected by the decline of the coal industry. After the survey, AGNC will compile a detailed report by fall 2025, incorporating feedback to create a balanced energy strategy with the help of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL).

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Aftermath of Pueblo’s homeless encampment and trash clear out, a week later](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [KOAA NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The City of Pueblo, led by Mayor Heather Graham, recently conducted a clean-up operation along Fountain Creek, removing 450 tons of trash and addressing homeless encampments, which has drawn mixed reactions from the community.
* Some residents support the clean-up for fostering a cleaner and more orderly environment, while others criticize the city for not providing adequate resources for the displaced homeless population.
* Despite available accommodations at the Pueblo Rescue Mission during the clean-up, no displaced individuals utilized these resources, raising concerns about the effectiveness of the city’s efforts to connect the homeless with support services.
* The city has allocated $16.6 million since 2021 for housing, homelessness, and infrastructure, yet challenges persist in matching the homeless with available services and support.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Mayor Mike Johnston unveils 2025 budget proposal amid cuts due to declining Denver consumer spending](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [CBS COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Denver Mayor Mike Johnston unveils the proposed 2025 budget, necessitating cuts due to a significant decrease in consumer spending, resulting in the city's lowest revenue growth since the pandemic at 1.1%.
* The budget proposes a $77 million reduction in the general fund, impacting migrant services, but allocates $215 million towards affordable housing and $74 million to Denver Health.
* Despite cuts, the budget prioritizes public safety, including training for new police recruits, firefighters, and deputies, and introduces initiatives for electric car charging stations and after-school programs.
* The Denver City Council is set to begin the approval process for the proposed budget next week, with a final approval deadline of November 12.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Trump announces new plan to end overtime taxes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [WASHINGTON EXAMINER](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Former President Donald Trump announced a plan to eliminate taxes on overtime pay for workers who log more than 40 hours per week, during a rally in Tucson, Arizona.
* Trump emphasized that this move aims to reward hard-working Americans and provide them with more incentive to work overtime.
* This proposal adds to his previous suggestions, including ending taxes on tips and Social Security benefits, targeting both restaurant workers and senior citizens in key swing states.
* The announcement follows a recent debate with Vice President Kamala Harris, where economic policies were a central theme, and Trump criticized the current administration's economic management.

[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|

**[Ganahl: Colorado’s ties to Kamala’s lies about later term abortion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY HEIDI GANAHL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_One of Kamala Harris’s most glaring falsehoods during the recent presidential debate was her dismissal of Donald Trump’s claim that abortion is legal and on demand at any point during pregnancy in some states.
